title: Maximum Profit of Operating a Centennial Wheel
statement:
You run a Ferris-style wheel whose gondola at ground level can take at most 4 riders. Turning the wheel once costs `runningCost`, and every rider pays `boardingCost` at the moment they get on.

`customers[i]` people join the line right before the wheel turns for the `i`-th time (0-indexed), so the wheel has already turned `i` times when they arrive. Before every turn, the people in line board the ground gondola, up to 4 of them; nobody may be left waiting while there is free room. Turns happen in sequence even when nobody boards (an empty turn still costs `runningCost`).

You may stop operating after any number of turns, even with people still in line; the turns needed afterwards to unload riders are free. The profit after `k` turns is `boardingCost` times the riders who boarded during those `k` turns, minus `k * runningCost`.

Return the **smallest** `k` whose profit is the largest possible. If no number of turns gives a strictly positive profit, return `-1`.
signature: int minOperationsMaxProfit(int[] customers, int boardingCost, int runningCost)
notes:
## Intuition

The profit only depends on how many people have boarded after each turn, and boarding is forced: whoever is in line gets on, four at a time. So there are no choices to make while running; the only decision is when to stop. Simulate the turns one by one, track the running profit, and remember the first turn where it hit a new maximum. A brute force would re-simulate the first `k` turns separately for every `k`, which repeats almost all the work.

## Approach

1. Keep `waiting` (people in line), `profit` (after the turns so far), and the best `bestProfit` / `bestRotations` seen, starting from `0` and `-1`.
2. Keep turning while there are arrivals still to come or people in line.
3. Before turn number `rotations`, add `customers[rotations]` to the line if that index exists.
4. Board `boarding = min(4, waiting)` people, then count the turn.
5. Update `profit` by `boarding * boardingCost - runningCost`.
6. Only a **strictly** larger profit replaces the best, so ties keep the earlier turn count, and a profit of `0` never counts.

## Example 1, step by step

`customers = [8, 3]`, `boardingCost = 5`, `runningCost = 6`.

- Turn 1: `waiting = 8`, 4 board, 4 remain; `profit = 20 - 6 = 14`, the new best at 1 turn.
- Turn 2: 3 arrive, `waiting = 7`, 4 board, 3 remain; `profit = 14 + 14 = 28`, best at 2 turns.
- Turn 3: no arrivals, 3 board; `profit = 28 + 15 - 6 = 37`, best at 3 turns.
- The line is empty and no one else comes, so the answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + S / 4), where S is the total number of customers; every turn either consumes an arrival index or boards people.
- Space: O(1); only a few counters.

## Pitfalls

- Turns with nobody boarding still cost `runningCost`, and they cannot be skipped while arrivals are still pending.
- Use `>` rather than `>=` so that equal profits keep the smaller number of turns.
- Do not stop the loop when the array ends: the people still in line keep boarding on later turns.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `waiting` | people currently in line |
| `boarding` | riders getting on during this turn (at most 4) |
| `rotations` | turns made so far |
| `profit` | profit after `rotations` turns |
| `bestProfit`, `bestRotations` | the best profit seen and the first turn count that reached it |

narration.2: Nobody is in line before the first turn.
narration.4: The best profit starts at 0, so only a strictly positive profit can ever be recorded.
narration.5: With no profitable stopping point yet, the answer would be -1.
narration.8: Keep turning while more groups will arrive or people are still in line.
narration.9: Group number rotations arrives just before this turn, if the array has one.
narration.10: Add the new arrivals to the line.
narration.12: At most four people fit in the gondola at ground level.
narration.15: Each rider pays boardingCost and the turn costs runningCost.
narration.16: Is this a strictly better profit than any earlier stopping point?
narration.18: ...and the number of turns that first reached it.
narration.21: Return the smallest turn count with the largest positive profit, or -1.
